To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression of a spatial network underlying task performance can differ across age groups as a function of extrinsic task difficulty, and this difference can influence the expression of task related fMR activation in older subjects.
the expression of a spatial pattern of activation during a recognition memory task is modulated by both task difficulty and age.
older adults show reduced efficiency and capacity in a network that is expressed during the performance of a task that is parametrically manipulated for difficulty.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the neural basis of cognitive aging and how it relates to the cognitive abilities of older adults.
the functional neuroanatomical basis of cognitive aging, and more specifically the relationship between age related changes in cognitive function and changes in the brain's functional organization.
understanding the neural mechanisms of cognitive ageing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is an age-related difference in the efficiency of a network underlying the performance of a task, and that this difference is modulated by the task demand, with the network being more efficient at the easier task levels in the old group, and at the more difficult task levels in the young group.
the efficiency of this brain network is reduced in the elderly.
the expression of a specific network underlying task performance varies as a function of both the intrinsic difficulty of the task and the extrinsic difficulty imposed by the task demands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain networks underlying cognitive task performance can vary as a result of task demand and that these changes may be differentially expressed across age groups.
task difficulty modulates young/old differences in network expression.
the brain networks underlying a task are expressed to a greater extent by older individuals when the task is easy, but to a lesser extent by older individuals as task difficulty is increased.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of a task related fMRI network can vary as a consequence of task difficulty.

when comparing the expression of a task related network across groups, it is necessary to consider the relative difficulty of a task for each group, because the expression of the network will depend on this.
task difficulty must be considered when comparing task performance and task-related brain activity across age groups.
